Hi Ben / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme Cloud is close to finalizing the template SOW and we have a couple of procurement checklist items that need concrete answers before we sign. We consolidated the most relevant SLO / monitoring questions below. A timely response will keep us on track to sign by end of month.

1) How do you measure uptime for the Redwood hosted API? Please describe the signal (success rate, upstream errors, timeouts) and the exact numerator/denominator.
2) For latency SLOs you list p95/p99 targets — are these based on observed server time excluding network hops, or end-to-end (client-to-backend)? What synthetic checks do you run and how often?
3) What monitoring access do customers get? Can we see per-route latency histograms, recent error traces, and raw token counts? Provide role & retention limits.
4) If Redwood needs a temporary exception (e.g., during a rollout), what is the formal process and what evidence do you provide to customers?
5) What is the timeline & format for SLO evidence deliverables (dashboard snapshot, raw export, signed attestation)?

We attached the procurement questionnaire (procurement@acmecloud.com) to this thread. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,

Sara — thanks for the clear list. I answered below inline and attached a short packet with a dashboard snapshot and our SLO evidence template. If you want a deeper technical walk-through we can schedule a 30-minute call this week.

1) Uptime signal: we measure request success rate at the Redwood API gateway. Numerator = successful 200-range responses from the inference runtime; denominator = total incoming inference requests accepted by the gateway (excluding client-side cancellations). We also separate user errors (4xx) in reporting. This aligns with our contractual uptime definition (availability = successful_requests / total_requests over the rolling 30-day window).

2) Latency basis: our contractual p95/p99 SLOs are measured server-side at the API boundary (time between request accepted and final token flush). We surface an end-to-end synthetic check that includes minimal client transport for region-level visibility; synthetic probes run every minute from three regions (us-east1, us-west1, eu-west1).

3) Customer monitoring access: read-only Grafana dashboards with per-route histograms (1s/10s/100s buckets), a link to recent error traces (sampled via trace id) for last 90 days, and daily token-usage CSV exports (30-day retention by default, extendable). Access is role-based (Viewer role) and limited to specified procurement/ops emails. For higher tiers we provide a short-term dashboard entitlement (14–30 days) with extended retention per the contract.

4) Temporary exceptions: exceptions are requested via the Customer Portal (Support -> SLA Requests). We require the following packet: (a) description of incident/change, (b) planned mitigation steps and timeline, (c) dashboard snapshot showing impact, (d) proposed compensating controls. We issue an exception record within 48 business hours and provide weekly updates until resolved. Exceptions that materially change the SLO terms need legal sign-off.

5) Evidence timeline & format: for procurement we provide a PDF snapshot of the Grafana views + a CSV export of raw aggregated metrics. For SOC/attestation requests we can also provide a signed statement that describes measurement methodology. Typical turnaround for a standard evidence packet is 3 business days.

Attachments: slo-evidence-snapshot.pdf, grafana-readonly-invite.txt

Let me know which specific dashboards or routes you want to see and I will provision Viewer access for the Acme contacts.

Thanks —
